title: Two identical MIDI devices collapse into one handle
body:
## Problem

`JavaMidiManager.MidiEndpoint` keys its registry of live handles by `MidiDeviceId(name, vendor)`, and `reconcile` folds the scanned devices into a map by that id, so when two devices of one direction share an id **only the one resolved last gets a handle** — the other is silently unreachable, with no log and no event.

Two units of the same model plugged in at once do share an id on macOS. CoreMIDI4J derives `name` from `kMIDIPropertyName`, `vendor` from `kMIDIPropertyManufacturer` and `description` from `kMIDIPropertyModel`, and hardcodes `version` to the literal `"Unknown Version"`, so all four `MidiDevice.Info` fields match. Nothing appends a port number or a counter. (`MidiDevice.Info` also makes `equals`/`hashCode` `final`, delegating to `Object`, so a provider cannot give it value semantics even if it wanted to.)

Note this is *not* the same as one bidirectional device appearing twice — that is already handled by the per-direction registries.

## A discriminator does exist, on macOS

`uk.co.xfactorylibrarians.coremidi4j.CoreMidiDeviceInfo` exposes `getEndPointUniqueID()` (also `getEntityUniqueID()` and `getdeviceUniqueID()`, plus session-scoped `get*Reference()` handles). CoreMIDI4J already keys its **own** device map by the endpoint UID, so two identical devices produce two distinct `MidiDevice` instances inside the library — the collapse happens only at our `MidiDeviceId`. macOS persists those UIDs in `~/Library/Preferences/ByHost/com.apple.MIDI.*.plist`, retaining them for devices that are currently offline. JUCE uses the same value as `MidiDeviceInfo.identifier`.

Off macOS there is nothing equivalent: CoreMIDI4J's non-macOS path delegates to `MidiSystem.getMidiDeviceInfo()` and detects change by comparing name/description/vendor/version tuples, and the JDK providers add only a package-private positional index.

## The UID must not go into `MidiDeviceId`

`MidiDeviceId` is serialized: `JsonCommonMidiFormat.midiDeviceIdFormat` is `Json.format[MidiDeviceId]`, used by `JsonTrackIOPluginFormat` for `DeviceTrackInputSpec` / `DeviceTrackOutputSpec` and by `JsonMtsTunerPluginFormating` for `altTuningOutput`, reaching `.tracks` files as `{"name": ..., "vendor": ...}`. Adding the UID there would:

1. put a machine-local integer into a shareable, human-editable document;
2. make it part of matching, `MidiDeviceId` being a `case class`, so a file that works today breaks after a MIDI-setup reset, on another machine, possibly on another USB port, and on every non-macOS platform;
3. make the file format platform-dependent.

The current id is imperfect but degrades gracefully; a UID would fail closed.

## Possible direction

Split identity the way JUCE does: `MidiDeviceId` stays the user-facing, serialized name, while the `javamidi` registries key on an **opaque platform key** obtained through the existing `JavaMidiEnvironment` seam — endpoint UID on macOS, a `(name, vendor, ordinal)` fallback elsewhere — keeping every CoreMIDI4J type inside `javamidi` per #282. Both units then get handles and both are enumerable.

This ripples: `MidiManager`'s whole per-direction API is keyed on `MidiDeviceId` (`openInput`/`openOutput`/`deviceHandleOf`/`deviceInfoOf`/the two device listings), and every `MidiEvent` carries one, with `TrackManager`, `Track` and their tests following. And it does not finish the job — a saved `.tracks` file still cannot say *which* of two identical devices it means, so resolution needs a documented tie-break plus a warning. The right fallback off macOS depends on #149.

### Make `MidiDeviceId` opaque

Rather than adding a field to it, make `MidiDeviceId` a **trait**, with the implementation owned by the platform layer — a `JavaMidiDeviceId` in `javamidi` holding whatever Java Sound and CoreMIDI4J can supply, the endpoint unique id included where it exists. A consumer should not know what identifies a device: only that it can compare two ids, display one, and hand one back to the `MidiManager`.

#### Is it already used as a black box?

Audited on `feature/hot-plug-midi-devices` at b625d98. **Consumers yes, the type itself no.**

Opaque at every call site outside `sc-midi`:

- Nothing in any module's `src/main` reads `name` or `vendor` off a `MidiDeviceId` — a search for field access on one returns no hit at all. (`cli`'s only `.vendor` is on `MidiDeviceInfo`, `MidiDevicesCommand.scala:47`, not on an id.)
- `tuner`, `app`, `ui` and `format` only compare ids, carry them in `MidiEvent`s and `TrackSpec`s, and hand them back to `MidiManager`. `TrackManager.tracksWithInputDevice` / `tracksWithOutputDevice` use `==` through `contains`.
- It is constructed in exactly two places in `src/main`: `JavaMidiConverters.asMidiDeviceId` (`JavaMidiConverters.scala:100`), which is the right boundary, and `MidiDeviceInfo.id` (`MidiDeviceInfo.scala:44`), which is not.

Not opaque in three places, one of them inside the type:

- **`MidiDeviceId.sanitizedName` (`MidiDeviceId.scala:47-48`) hardcodes CoreMIDI4J.** It strips the `"CoreMIDI4J - "` prefix using `MidiDeviceId.CoreMidi4JDeviceNamePrefix` (`:58`), so the platform-agnostic `org.calinburloiu.music.scmidi` package already names a CoreMIDI4J detail, against the isolation #282 draws. It has **no production caller** — only `MidiDeviceIdTest` — even though its ScalaDoc says "Use this name instead of the actual name in user interfaces".
- **`format` serializes it structurally** (see below).
- **`MidiDeviceInfo.id`** builds one from a name and a vendor in that same platform-agnostic package.

So the trait split is not only room for the endpoint unique id: it repays an isolation breach that exists today.

#### What would have to change

- **`format` needs a hand-written `Format`.** `JsonCommonMidiFormat.midiDeviceIdFormat` is `Json.format[MidiDeviceId]` (`JsonCommonMidiFormat.scala:25`), used by `JsonTrackIOPluginFormat` (`:41`) and `JsonMtsTunerPluginFormating` (`:37`), so the JSON shape follows the fields. Besides the `Format` itself, this forces a decision about what a `.tracks` file names and which implementation a read produces — the same question the endpoint unique id raises above, so the two are one decision rather than two.
- **`sanitizedName` moves into the `javamidi` implementation**, where the prefix it strips comes from. Worth settling at the same time whether the UI should be calling it at all, since nothing does.
- **`MidiDeviceInfo.id` becomes abstract or moves**, it being the second construction site in the platform-agnostic package.
- **Equality stops being the case class's structural equality** and becomes the implementation's, which `correspondsToInfo` (`MidiDeviceId.scala:37`) and both registries rely on. Two ids from different implementations must have a defined answer.
- **12 test files construct `MidiDeviceId(name, vendor)` directly**, so they need a concrete implementation or a test factory.

## Interim mitigations (not done)

- Log a warning in `MidiEndpoint.reconcile` when the fold drops a device, so the failure is diagnosable rather than silent, and note the limitation in `docs/architecture/sc-midi/README.md`.
- Users can rename one unit in Audio MIDI Setup: the persisted MIDI setup holds an editable per-device `name`, so the two ids then differ and everything works unchanged.

## Not verified

- The collision on real hardware — reproducing it needs two identical devices. It is inferred from CoreMIDI4J's name-construction source, which is unambiguous.
- UID stability across unplug/replug, a different USB port, and a reboot. The persisted plist retains the UIDs and keeps offline device records, which is strong but indirect evidence; a different USB port is the case most likely to break it, the persisted USB records being keyed on location id, vendor/product and a serial number that identical class-compliant devices may leave blank.

Found while reviewing #304 (#131 / #288): `reconcile`'s comment already states that the device resolved last wins.
